description: The provided image is a multi-layered pie chart illustrating the ethical principles and corresponding duties within medical ethics, likely serving as a conceptual framework for the MedEthicsQA benchmark. The chart is organized into four primary ethical pillars—Beneficence (blue), Autonomy (green), Non-Maleficence (purple), and Justice (orange)—each represented as a large segment of the inner circle. Radiating outward from each pillar are numerous sub-segments, each labeled with a specific ethical duty or guideline. For example, under Beneficence, duties include “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” and “Ethical research.” Under Autonomy, duties include “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed,” “Maintain Confidential Communication,” and “Professional Relationship with Patients and Their Relatives.” Non-Maleficence includes “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Report Unethical and Unprofessional Conduct,” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain.” Justice encompasses “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” and “Promote Environmental Sustainability.” The chart visually emphasizes the breadth and granularity of ethical considerations in medicine, with each sub-segment proportionally sized to reflect its conceptual weight or frequency within the framework, though exact percentages are not provided. This structure likely underpins the question categories in the MedEthicsQA benchmark, enabling systematic evaluation of LLMs’ understanding across core domains of medical ethics.
